{Phi '93) and Theodore Leland Waugh (Pi '98) for the term expiring
1917. Bros. Babst and Waugh were thereupon duly elected.

Bro. Salisbury (Chi) reported for the Committee on Annual Com
munication the following resolutions :

I. Approving the report of the Treasurer.
II. Authorizing the Executive Council to take up the matter of
permanent mailing lists of all members of Psi Upsilon.

The resolutions were separately and unanimously adopted. (General
Resolutions Nos. 6 and 7.)

President Bridgman then took the Chair.

The Recorder read a telegram from Bro. President William Howard
Taft (Beta '78).*

(Kappa) reported for the Committee on New Business the

III.
Disapproving a Traveling Secretary and suggesting more

RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED

GENEEAL EESOLUTIONS

General Resolution No. 1 

Whereas, Psi Upsilon Alumni have
"
volunteered to undertake the formation of a Committee on Business
"
Information for the benefit of members of the Fraternity ; and

Whereas, It is highly desirable that this offer should be accepted
and given cordial support throughout the Fraternity, as a means of
common helpfulness and encouragement ;

Therefore, Be It Resolved, That the Executive Council be author
ized to nominate annually a Committee of five or more Psi Upsilon

Alumni, who shall have their headquarters at New York City, and be
Committee on Business Information," with such
"

designated as the
powers and duties as shall be committed to it from time to time by the
Council. The Committee shall annually make a report to the Council,
which shall be included as part of the Annual Communication of the
Executive Council to the Convention.

General Resolution No. 2 

Resolved, That the Seventy-ninth Con
vention put itself on record as being opposed to the establishment of
chapters outside the present territorial dominion; and therefore be it

Resolved, That the Convention take action unfavorably in regard
to the petition of the Chi Delta Psi Fraternity of Toronto University
for a charter of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.

General Resolution No. 8 

Whereas, In accordance with established
precedents of the Fraternity a petition for a charter must be signed by
the individual petitioners; and

Whereas, The petition of the Pi Upsilon Fraternity of the Uni
versity of Kansas is signed only by the President of the Society;

Therefore, Be It Resolved, That the petition of the Pi Upsilon
Fraternity of the University of Kansas be denied by this Convention.

General Resolution No. 4:Resolved, That the petition of the Phi
Kappa Society of the University of Washington be denied by this Con
vention owing to a lack of information, but in the judgment of the
Convention it is desirable to have a Chapter as a companion to the
Epsilon whenever a suitable opportunity may present itself.

10

General Resolution No. 5 

Resolved, That this Convention take im
mediate and favorable action upon the petition of the Delta Delta
Society of Williams College.
General Resolution No. 6

Resolved, That the report of the Treasurer
of the Executive Council be and hereby is approved.

General Resolution No. 7 

Resolved, That the Executive Council be
and hereby is authorized to take up the matter of keeping permanent
mailing lists of all members of Psi Upsilon, as suggested by Bro. Keppel
(Lambda '98), providing that such lists shall contain the names and
addresses(including street numbers in cities) of aU members of the
Fraternity.

General Resolution No. 8 

Resolved, That a Committee be appointed
by the President of the Executive Council to investigate the matter of
renewing the publication of the Diamond.

General Resolution No. 9 

Resolved, That hereafter Conventions of
this Fraternity be held within the flrst two weeks of May unless cir
cumstances justify a change of date, in which case a part of July or

August shall be utili^ied.

General Resolution No. 10 Resolved^ That this Convention shaU

not entertain any idea which has been suggested of a Traveling Secre
tary, and believes that the same results may be obtained by a more
regular visitation of the Chapters by the members of the Executive
Council.

SPECIAL eesolutions

Special Resolution No. 1 Resolved, That the Recorder be requested

to convey to the Lambda Chapter the thanks of the Convention for
their hospitality and congratulations upon their efficient management of
the Convention.

Special Resolution No. 2 Resolved, That the thanks of the Con

vention be tendered to the Psi Upsilon Club of the City of New York
for their hospitality in providing the Smoker at Terrace Garden last

Constitutional Amendment. The Convention of 1911 adopted a
Resolution {General Resolution No. 2) to amend Article III of the
Constitution by adding thereto a new section, as follows :

When a Chapter has been or shall be estabUshed
Section 5.
upon application of undergraduate students belonging to an or
ganization comprising undergraduate and graduate or retired
members, it shall be lawful for such Chapter by unanimous vote
to elect graduate or retired members of such organization in good

standing upon their written application, and to initiate them in
due form.

No objection to the Resolution having been reported by any Chap
ter the amendment has become effective.

SiLVEB Wedding at the White House. On the occasion of the
celebration at the White House, June 19, 1911, of the twenty-fifth an
niversary of the wedding of Brother William Howard Taft, Beta, '78,
the Council, in the name of the Fraternity, presented to the President
and Mrs. Taft a handsome silver salver, appropriately engraved, which
was duly acknowledged in a letter expressing thanks and appreciation.

A full size photograph of the salver was preserved for the archives, and
a half size photograph was sent to each Chapter.

Intee-Featernitt Confeeence. In the Annual Communication to
the Convention of 1910, and again in 1911, attention was called to the in
vitation to our Fraternity to participate in the Conference of Greek Let
ter Societies. By General Resolution No. 1 of 1911, the Convention au
"
thorized the Council to notify the Inter- Fraternity Conference as
they
shall see fit," and directed the delegates to notify their Chapters that the
"
Council should receive an immediate response from the Chapters in
regard to this matter." Special request for expression of opinion was
contained in the letter of the Recorder transmitting to the Chapters
the printed minutes of the Council meeting of October 9, 1911, and
again in November the Council, through the Secretary, requested the
advice of the Chapters, stating that the conference of 1911 would occur
on December 2 and that the Fraternity had been invited to
participata
Up to the hour of the Conference only nine chapters had replied (three

13

in favor, six against), and the secretary of the Conference was noti
fied that the Council did not feel at liberty to participate. Of the
Chapters that have reported their views on the subject of joining the
Conferences those in favor were: Delta, Beta, Xi, Iota, Chi and Rho;
those opposed: Gamma, Kappa, Psi, Upsilon, Phi^ Pi, Tau, Epsilon
and Omicron; undecided: Theta, Sigma, Eta, Omega. No response was
received from Zeta, Lambda, Beta Beta, Mu.

Printed copies of the proceedings of the Conference of 1911 were
sent by the Council to all the Chapters. In view of the divided senti
ment of the Chapters as thus far indicated, the Council will take no

part in proceedings of the Inter-Fraternity Conference. The Council
would, however, commend to the Chapters a careful consideration of
the published minutes of the Conference and of the work and methods
proposed by its members promote and maintain the efficiency of
to
the Greek Letter Societies. Some, at least, of the suggestions made
may be usefully adoijted by our own Fraternity.

Iota Chaptbe Delinquent. The Council regrets the necessity of
reporting that the Iota Chapter failed to pay its annual dues to the
treasury of the Fraternity for 1912 within the time prescribed, and
under Article II, section 2, of the Constitution is not entitled to rep
resentation at the Convention.

Mastees of the Rolls. It seems necessary to remind the Chap
ters again of the Resolution adopted by the Convention of 1902, pro
viding for the annual appointment of three officers known as Masters
of the Rolls, one graduate and two iindergraduates, who, shall be charged
with the duty, among other things, of keeping the addresses of mem
bers up to date. The practical importance of their functions is obvious.
If properly performed, not only the Chapters, but the Fraternity, will
be greatly benefited. Several of the Chapters have already adopted the
practice of printing annual revisions of their lists in booklet form for
distribution. Some of the National Fraternities have salaried secre

taries for the purpose of keeping their membership list up to date, and
at least one Fraternity of larger membership than ours owns the type
from which its last general catalogue was printed and keeps it in form
for changes of address as they occur. We may not perhaps expect
such perfection of accuracy, but If each Chapter would make a deter
mined and persistent effort to keep track of its own members it
would benefit the Fraternity in many ways. If possible, the graduate

14

members of the Masters of the Rolls should serve for a number of

years, and the undergraduate members at least two years, and the
card Indexes should be
kept reliable by every available resource.
According to the Annual Reports for 1912 only five of the Chapters
have three Masters of the Rolls, Delta, Gamma, Kappa, Iota and
Pi; twelve have two, Theta, Sigma, Zeta, Lambda, Psi, Upsilon,
Beta Beta, Eta, Tau, Mu, Epsilon and Omicron ; two have only one,
Xi and Rho ; and four have none, Beta, Phi, Chi and Omega.

Application for Applications for charters have been
Chaetbes.
received from the members Society of Williams Col
of Delta Delta
lege and of the Pi Upsilon Society of the University of Kansas, and
are herewith submitted. The Council has been advised that applica
tions will be presented by the Chi Delta Psi Society of the University
of Toronto, Canada, and by the Phi Kappa Society of the University
of Washington.

The Council. At the last convention Brother George Henry Fox

(Upsilon, '67) was elected to succeed himself for the term expiring
1916, and Brother Frederick Paul Keppel (Lambda, '98) was elected
for the same term to succeed Brother Shattuck (Lambda, '99). Brother
Edward Livingston Stevens (Chi, '99) was elected for the term end

ing 1913 in place of Brother Saxe (Lambda, '00), resigned.

The officers of the Council
during the past year have been : Presi
dent, Brother
Bridgman; Secretary, Brother Coleman; Treasurer,
Brother Poole; Recorder, Brother Whiting; Archivist, Brother Fisher.
Ten meetings have been held and copies of the minutes have been
regularly mailed to the Chapters.

The terms of Brothers Babst (Phi, '93) and Fisher (Beta, '96)
expire this year, and it will be necessary for the Convention to elect
two members of the Council for the term ending 1917.

Alumni Associations. During the year the Council has endeavored
to secure a list of the Psi
Upsilon Alumni Associations and has ar
ranged to send to them copies of the minutes of the meetings for the
purpose of keeping them in touch with Fraternity affairs. It is hoped
that each Association will find it convenient annually to celebrate
Founders' Day (November 24). A good beginning in this direction
was made last year.

15

Student Standing of Feateenity Men. The Council feels com

pelled to call the attention of the Convention to the general discus
sion now proceeding in the Academic world as to the student standing
of Greek Letter Fraternity men as compared with the general student
standing prevailing in their University or College. As one of the
oldest and most conservative of the Greek Letter Fraternities Psi
Upsilon has met its responsibility in this important matter by con
tinuing and strictly adhering to its traditional policy of accepting
" "
and encouraging men of the all around type, but who also recognize
scholarship and student standing as an integral and controlling factor
in a college education.
Any Chapter whose average student standing falls below the aver
age standing prevailing in its University or College has turned away
from the traditions and purposes of Psi Upsilon and should change
its course at once as a matter of justice to itself, to its sister Chapters
and to the Fraternity as a whole.
The Executive Council has given much consideration to this mat
ter and considers it a responsibility of growing importance, and recom
mends that the Chapters regard it in the same light.

Business Connections. At the May meeting of the Council an

oral report was presented on the method of various college fraternities
and alunmi associations for keeping in touch with those desiring posi
tions in the business or professional world and with parties requiring
services. It was thought that a plan might be devised to the mutual
advantage of members of Psi Upsilon, and the Council will present
the matter to the Convention for consideration.

Treasueee's Rbpobt. The report of the Treasurer is submitted
herewith.
